minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard schools and town manager on FY23 needs and set an Oct 7 review of special town meeting articles.
minutes.summary: The committee held its informal pre-budget talk with the superintendent and school business director, covering Test and Stay, ESSER-funded positions, staffing, busing and IT. The town manager then reviewed FY23 general government needs, capital projects and draft special town meeting articles. The committee agreed to add a meeting on October 7 and voted only to adjourn.

votes.motion: Adjourn the meeting, by roll call
votes.outcome: passed; roll call all in favor

budget_items.what_was_said: The state pays for test materials; staffing reimbursement is unknown. Local funds cover clerical support at first, possibly shifting to ESSER later.
A member noted much of the new hiring is temporary grant money and asked for clear visibility of which positions are grant-funded versus tax-funded.
The fourth-year option came in far above earlier years, so the district will not exercise it and will rebid in January.
The assessor submitted new growth above the town meeting estimate, which would eliminate a deficit from school choice and charter assessments.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee added a meeting on October 7 to review draft special town meeting articles, with the public hearing set for October 14.
The town manager said the assessor's new growth came in above the town meeting estimate, which would eliminate a deficit from school choice and charter assessments.
The district will not exercise the bus contract's fourth-year option because it came in far above earlier years, and will rebid in January.
A member asked for clear visibility of which new positions are temporary ESSER grant-funded and which are tax-funded.
Earmarks were added to the October 7 agenda and a joint meeting with the School Committee on Chapter 70 was set for October 28; the only vote was to adjourn.

why_it_matters: Whether school positions are paid by temporary ESSER grants or by taxes decides what lands on the tax bill when the grant money ends.
The new growth figure, the bus rebid and the special town meeting articles (including a higher elderly exemption abatement) all bear on what the town has to raise from taxes for FY23.
